sections.markdown:
## Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Motorcyclists share the traffic rights and responsibilities of other drivers but are more physically exposed in a collision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
A motorcycle's smaller outline can make it appear farther away or slower than it is. Check again at intersections and check blind spots directly before changing lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
Give a motorcycle the full lane; do not share that lane while driving beside or passing it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
A rider may change position within the lane to improve visibility or avoid a hazard. That position change alone does not establish an intention to turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
Potholes, gravel, slippery surfaces, seams, rail crossings and grooved pavement may cause a rider to change speed or lane position suddenly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A01
Before entering a motorcycle's path, make sure the rider's maneuver has actually begun. A motorcycle's flashing signal may have been left on rather than indicating the next turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A01
The handbook recommends a following interval of 3 or 4 seconds behind a motorcycle, with additional space to avoid abrupt braking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A01
When a motorcycle passes your vehicle, maintain lane position and speed to let the rider complete the pass and regain a normal lane position. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A01
When passing a motorcycle, use a full adjacent lane and leave enough room before returning so the rider is not forced to swerve. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A02
Traffic approaching a school bus stopped for loading or unloading generally must stop. With a dividing median, opposite-side traffic is excepted, while traffic following or beside the bus in its direction must stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A02
After stopping for a school bus, wait until it resumes moving or deactivates the warnings, and until all passengers loading or unloading have cleared the roadway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A02
Large trucks are longer, heavier and harder to maneuver than cars and require additional room for turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A02
The handbook calls a truck or bus's enlarged blind areas the no-zones, including areas beside, behind and in front of it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A02
Before towing, use suitable equipment, stay within the towing capacity, distribute weight appropriately and secure the load. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A02
Inspect and maintain both tow vehicle and trailer, become familiar with handling through practice, and consider tow mirrors or other needed safety equipment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A02
Allow time when trailering and remain calm if control is lost; the handbook's brief checklist is not a complete towing procedure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A03
A truck or bus has large blind areas on both sides. If its driver's face is not visible in the side mirror, do not assume the driver can see your vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A03
The right-side blind area is especially hazardous because large vehicles may need a wide right turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A03
Avoid following closely in a large vehicle's rear blind area; you may be unseen and unable to see traffic conditions ahead of it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A03
Large vehicles need extra stopping room. Do not merge closely in front of a truck or bus and then reduce speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A03
Before moving into the lane ahead of a truck or bus, make sure its entire front is visible in your rearview mirror. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A03
Give a commercial vehicle ample space during highway entry and merging, and avoid cutting it off, tailgating or speeding around it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=46]

Misconceptions: A bicycle may lawfully use a full lane; a motorcycle signal or lane position alone does not prove that its rider will turn.
Mnemonic: See the person, leave room, wait for the conflict to clear.
Glossary: A no-zone is an area around a large vehicle where visibility or maneuvering creates added danger; an unmarked crosswalk follows an intersection's sidewalk crossing.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Penalty schedules, unsupported statistical comparisons and diagram-based gesture recognition remain debt rather than learner claims.

Pedestrian death statistics, exact speed-versus-fatality percentages and image charts are withheld pending current evidence.
The bicycle fallback-speed comparison and fine repeat the earlier ambiguous wording; the exact numeric speed comparison is withheld pending clarification.
Bicycle arm-position drawings are image-only; no gesture-to-direction mapping is inferred from the extraction.

School-bus warning wording here mentions red or amber in advance and is less precise than the earlier yellow-warning/red-stop account; no rule requiring a stop solely for advance amber is inferred. Color-phase reconciliation remains debt.

School-bus penalties, truck weight/stopping-distance ratios, vehicle-class rear-mirror generalizations, citation statistics and the fixed car-length-per-speed spacing rule are withheld pending current technical or legal review.
Commercial-vehicle diagrams, the mobile-app advertisement and external trailering guidance are not reproduced or treated as inspected evidence.
